text:
Vegas is 14-6-5, has lost in regulation once in its last ten (5-1-4), and the underlying play backs it up. The Golden Knights have 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), their points match their play almost exactly, and we give them a 97% chance at the playoffs and close to even odds (48%) of winning the Pacific.

The penalty kill is the quiet strength. Vegas allows just 0.48 expected goals a game shorthanded, and it draws more penalties than it takes. Brayden McNabb and Shea Theodore have logged 379 minutes together at 5v5 and won 58% of the expected goals, with 22 goals for and 16 against.

Up front, the Las Vegas Review-Journal called the Ivan Barbashev experiment over: he is back with Jack Eichel and Mark Stone, and that line has outscored opponents 10-4 at 5v5. Victor Olofsson, in his second stint in Vegas, has 10 points in his last 10 games (6.8 expected).

The questions are small ones. The Nic Dowd checking line gets only 34% of the expected goals, and the Rasmus Andersson and Jeremy Lauzon pair 42%. In Saturday's 5-4 shootout win in Winnipeg, Carter Hart gave up a goal on the first shot for the second start in a row, and The Athletic's Jesse Granger noted the third period keeps being a struggle. Adin Hill, meanwhile, is 3.8 goals better than expected over his last five starts.
